claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship an upgrade path with the component; a migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
Component state migrations are a new Pulumi feature.
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
A component state migrations discussion exists at github.com/pulumi/pulumi/discussions/24799.
The v1 example uses the legacy `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc` component, creating a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and association, and an internet gateway.
Replacing an AWS VPC forces replacement of a security group that refers to the VPC's ID (per AWS CloudFormation EC2 SecurityGroup VpcId docs).
A replacement database does not automatically contain the old data; deleting the old database without backup or data migration could lose that data.
The second version of the example upgrades to the modern `awsx.ec2.Vpc` component while keeping the existing network.
The third version removes AWSX and declares resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three example versions, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.
Pulumi state records each resource and component with a URN, and managed resources also have a provider ID.
The legacy AWSX component wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components; modern AWSX removes those wrappers; the subnet's Pulumi name changes from `vpc-isolated-0` to `vpc-isolated-1`.
Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when saved state remains compatible, but cannot remove component wrappers and transfer references.
A Pulumi component registers a migration callback via the `stateMigrations` resource option, together with an alias for the legacy component type.

The state migration callback receives the aliased component's saved state followed by its children's state, and returns `newState` (complete set of replacement records) and `successors` (map from each disappearing old URN to its replacement URN).
The example's `rename` helper copies the saved record and changes its URN, type, and parent while preserving the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.
Pulumi uses `successors` mappings to update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, keeping the security group's VPC reference connected to the migrated VPC.

Pulumi runs multiple state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next; a legacy AWSX stack can upgrade directly to plain AWS, a modern AWSX stack skips the first migration, and after both have run the callbacks return no result on later updates.
After a migration Pulumi compares the new program with the migrated state and calls the provider for remaining changes; the example can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
Preview evaluates the state migration without saving it, and the update saves the migrated state; the existing resources should show no creates, deletes, or replacements.
When a component author registers the migration inside the component, users need not write the migration or edit stack state; Pulumi runs it during normal preview and update.
The component state migrations guide at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/state-migrations/ covers the callback contract, and the VPC example contains all three programs.
State migration callbacks (the stateMigrations resource option) run during Pulumi previews and updates when prior state exists.
State migration callbacks must be idempotent and return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
State migration callbacks rewrite state without performing provider operations.
A Pulumi component state migration callback is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A Pulumi component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
In a component state migration result, each successor mapping connects an old URN omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a component state migration callback returns no result.
Component state migration state entries use the checkpoint resource format, including fields such as urn, type, id, parent, provider, inputs, and outputs.
A component state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using update plans or targeted updates.
The restrictions on state-changing migration results (with update plans or targeted updates) do not require removing an already-applied migration.
The option reference at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/#callback-api explains the callback API.
